overall_summary: Extreme exoplanet anomalies and first-person 'What If You Fell Into...' survival/exploration hooks dominate channel engagement and reach (averaging 700-1,000+ views with 20-38 likes). Conversely, repeated psychology factoids (earworms, fake memories) and generic science trivia (silent space, shark age) suffer from severe audience fatigue and low retention.

winning_patterns.pattern: First-Person Peril / 'What If You Fell Into...' Extreme Planetary Scenarios
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes) drive peak viewership and engagement.
winning_patterns.action: Adopt visceral, second-person narrative framing ('You step out...', 'If you jumped...') focused on extreme cosmic environments.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos running 19-21 seconds covering mind-bending celestial physics (TrES-2b Darker than Coal: 1,031 views; Venus Day/Year: 981 views; Supersonic Rubies: 725 views) consistently outperform short 12-16s snippets.
winning_patterns.action: Standardize video length to 20-21 seconds to provide adequate suspense pacing and sensory payoff.

weak_patterns.evidence: Repeated uploads of 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5 to 53 views) and song loop psychology (17 to 71 views) generated negligible interest.
weak_patterns.action: Halt repetitive brain trivia unless framed as an immersive, narrative psychological horror micro-case.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' posted 3 times plateaued at 34-220 views; Octopus heart facts yielded minimal organic traction relative to exoplanet content.
weak_patterns.action: Cease reposting over-saturated middle-school trivia without a radical fresh angle or cinematic tension.

next_video.hook_style: Second-person lethal scenario with immediate physical consequence
next_video.concept: What would happen to the human body when approaching a Magnetar
next_video.opening_direction: Start with a camera rapidly hurtling toward a blinding, hyper-spinning cosmic lighthouse with the hook: 'If you drifted within 1,000 miles of a magnetar, you wouldn't crash—your body would instantly dissolve.'
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that the magnetic field is so unfathomably strong (trillions of times Earth's) that it literally distorts the electron clouds of your atoms, turning your body into stretched, microscopic needles before you even touch the surface.
next_video.reason: Leverages the proven high-engagement 'What If You Fell Into' visceral survival framework while introducing an untouched, terrifying cosmic phenomenon (Magnetar) to avoid topic cannibalization.
